summary: Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi was an Indologist. He served as a Jain Pandit at the Central Library of Vadodara and held a post at the Oriental Institute, Baroda (attested 1939).

Lama Jabb is a Tibetologist. He served as a Junior Research Fellow at the University of Oxford and held the post of Head of the Tibetan & Himalayan Studies Centre at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

Lama Jampa Thaye is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from the University of Manchester (~1986–1990) and studied under several traditional teachers, later joining the international teaching faculty at Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.

Lama Kunga Rinpoche is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ngor E-Vam Choden Monastery, where he served as Thartse Shabthung in 1959, and founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center in 1973.

Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (1946–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dungkar Monastery and under numerous teachers, founded Kopan Monastery and the FPMT, and served as spiritual director of the FPMT from 1984.
Lama Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and with the traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued traditional studies under Lama Norlha and Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996).

Lambert Schmithausen is an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker. He was an associate professor of Indology at the University of Münster (1970–1973) and served on the University of Hamburg Advisory Board (1973–2005).

Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at McMaster University in 1986 and served as a professor at the University of San Diego (attested 1997).

Lance S. Cousins (1942–2015) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey and K. R. Norman. He taught at Manchester (~1970–1998) and Oxford (~2000–2015), and was president of the Pali Text Society (2002–2003).
Lang Chen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Chen completed a PhD at Yale University, studying under Janet Gyatso, Koichi Shinohara, and Phyllis Granoff.

Lang Eun Ra is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Ra completed doctoral studies at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu, also studying under Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert M. Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.

Lara Braitstein is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and became Associate Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism there (attested 2026).
Laren Hogen Bays is a Buddhist and religious studies specialist. Having studied under traditional teacher Shōdō Harada, Bays co-founded and served as co-abbot of the Great Vow Zen Monastery.

Larry DeVries is a religious studies and Indology scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Minnesota. He taught at Minnesota, Washington, and Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, held a research post at Chicago, and was at Langara College (attested 2005).

Lars Fogelin is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli, later holding positions at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.
Lars Martin Fosse is an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg University, the University of Bonn, and the University of Oslo (~1974–1997). He also taught at the University of Oslo (attested 2002).

Lata Chhatre specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She served as a Reader (attested 2009) and as Visiting Faculty (attested 2026) in the Department of Philosophy at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Lati Rinpoche (1922–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Ganden and Gyuto monasteries. He served as abbot of Ganden Monastery (~1976–1985), taught at Namgyal Monastery (1976), and was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia (1976).
Latika Lahiri is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji in 1958 as an Indian Government scholar and held a post at the University of Delhi.
